How to get into rockettry without spending tons of money

Engines are cheaper to buy than make, trust me on this. To do it properly and safely requires a lot of upfront cost in testing tools and trial and error.

The rockets themselves can be simmed in openrocket which can then print out fin templates and such. So you can buy balsa or thing plywood at hobby shops and cut your own fins and such.

Tubes can be made with white or wood glue an rolling up copy paper over a mandrel, thing a 3/4 in broomstick handle.

You can carve nosecones out of Styrofoam. Or caste them with hobby store casting supplied.

Or buy from Estesrockets.com when they have a sale.

Carbon Footprint of Cloth and Disposable Diapers is Equal?!?

I've read a lot of conflicting information on this subject. The study cited in this article does take into consideration many factors of the manufacturing and maintenance of diapers, but it said the impact of extra electricity, and waste from detergent and softeners makes cloth just as bad for the environment. I don't think these people actually use cloth diapers. Line drying works for me most days. If it's too humid out, I hang them inside near an air vent. I only use non-toxic laundry soap. And softener ruins diapers! Taking all these factors into consideration, I don't think cloth is as damaging to environment. Thoughts?

My wife and i never looked into the environmental impact when choosing whether to go cloth or not; we were more focused on price and ease of use. We ended up ordering disposable diapers through honest.com. They are fully degradable and neither of us were very excited about the concept of washing diapers.

I think you might be right in your case about cloth being less damaging. There are a lot of factors to consider though, like you mentioned; what kind of laundry soap are parents using? Do they live in a climate where they can air dry them?

Yes there are many factors to consider. As far as price goes, I don't think there's much argument against cloth being the winner. My cloth paid for itself vs the price of diapering with Luvs within six months.

It was the same for my family. The cost savings made my decision for me. I have to think that cloth diapers have made less of an impact environmentaly as well. I used the same detergent and I never use softeners or dryer sheets anyway because of the carcinogens they contain. Woolzies dryer balls take their place.
I use wool dryer balls too! They're great.
